newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Hun Sen troops reach Cambodian royalist stronghold.
newsitem.headline: Hun Sen troops reach Cambodian royalist stronghold.

text.p: Troops under Cambodia's Second Prime Minister Hun Sen have moved into the northern town of Samrong, the last town held by royalist forces loyal to the country's ousted first prime minister, officials said on Saturday.
The troops arrived peacefully and negotiations with royalist forces were under way in the town, near the border with Thailand, the government officials said.
"We don't occupy it completely. Up to now we are negotiating with them to hand over their weapons," secretary of state for information, Khieu Kanharith, told Reuters.
"I can confirm that our men are there and they got there without fighting," he said.
Defence Ministry spokesman Chum Sambath said talks were underway with the royalist forces' main commander in the area, General Khann Savoeun.
"The government has a policy to appeal to our brothers to come back," he said.

Fighting broke out between forces loyal to Cambodia's rival co-prime ministers on July 5 in Phnom Penh. Hun Sen ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh the following day after Hun Sen took complete control of the capital.

Hun Sen's forces and those loyal to Ranariddh began fighting in northern Cambodia near the town of Siem Reap, home to the Angkor Wat temple complex, soon after but the royalist forces were swiftly pushed back towards Samrong.
In several other areas of the country, Hun Sen's forces and royalist troops negotiated local ceasefire deals.
A senior member of Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party said in Bangkok on Friday that armed resistance to Hun Sen was a last resort.
"The prince does not want to have bloodshed. The first solution is to get Hun Sen to negotiate," royalist member of parliament Ahmad Yahaya said.
"If we don't achieve this, as a final solution we would have to create a resistance movement," he said.

Royalist forces and Hun Sen were on opposing sides during the 1980s when royalist troops, in an alliance with the Khmer Rouge guerrilla group and a smaller non-communist force, battled Hun Sen and his Hanoi-backed government in Phnom Penh.
After years of tortuous negotiations, the warring factions signed a peace treaty in 1991, paving the way for United Nations-run elections in 1993 which Ranariddh won.
